label: Ischemia, Injury, Infarction: the Ladder
rows: Often the VERY FIRST sign of ischemia. Broad, tall, SYMMETRICAL (big enough to hold the QRS). Normal T = asymmetrical, slow upstroke, sharper fall. Easily missed: no ST change to call yet.
SUBENDOCARDIAL ischemia (inner layer). Often GLOBAL, in nearly every lead.

INFARCTION: death of tissue, from a previous OR an acute event. Longer than 0.04 s (one small box) AND deeper than 2 mm, or more than 25% of the R wave. No R wave = QS complex, still pathologic in an infarction.
No slide. In lecture: a sign of ischemia, LATER than hyperacute T waves.

label: J Point & Baseline
rows: Junction of the QRS and the ST segment. ST segment = J point to onset of the T wave. Healthy heart: both AT BASELINE.
Acute coronary syndrome can push the J point ABOVE (ST elevation) or BELOW (ST depression) the baseline.
Compare the J point with the TP SEGMENT. Fast rate, no TP segment: compare with the ONSET OF THE QRS.

label: Coronary Arteries
rows: Divides into the CIRCUMFLEX and the LEFT ANTERIOR DESCENDING.
Right atrium, RIGHT VENTRICLE, BOTTOM (inferior) of the left ventricle, back of the septum. ★ Inferior wall = right coronary (about 80-85% of people, said in lecture).
FRONT (and bottom) of the left ventricle, FRONT of the septum → septal, anterior, anteroseptal infarction.
Left atrium, SIDE and BACK of the left ventricle → lateral, high lateral, POSTERIOR infarction.
Return used, oxygen-poor blood to the right atrium.

label: Leads → Wall → Reciprocal
rows: I, aVL, V5, V6 · reciprocal II, III, aVF
I, aVL, V3-V6 · reciprocal II, III, aVF
II, III, aVF · reciprocal I, aVL (right coronary)
I, aVL · reciprocal III, aVF (circumflex in lecture; a diagonal of the left anterior descending can also supply it)
The only lead with no wall assigned.
Lead III and lead aVL (in lecture).

label: ST-Elevation Infarction & Reciprocal Changes
rows: 1 mm or more in 2 or more CONTIGUOUS leads, with or without reciprocal changes. (V2-V3 thresholds are higher, given in lecture: women 1.5 mm, men 40 and over 2 mm, men under 40 2.5 mm.)
Mirror image on the OPPOSITE leads. ST depression with ST elevation on the same tracing = ALWAYS reciprocal.
Reciprocal changes CONFIRM ischemia when ST elevation is present; their ABSENCE does NOT exclude it.

label: Posterior Leads & V4R
rows: ISOLATED ST depression in V1-V4 with NO elevation anywhere = reciprocal of a POSTERIOR infarction until proven otherwise. Obtain posterior leads.
Move V4, V5, V6 to the BACK as V7, V8, V9 (the 15-lead). ST ELEVATION there confirms. 3-4% of infarctions; LEFT CIRCUMFLEX.
Inferior infarction (RIGHT CORONARY) + HYPOTENSION, CLEAR LUNGS, JUGULAR VEIN DISTENSION → suspect right ventricular involvement.
V4 to the RIGHT 5th intercostal space, midclavicular line. ELEVATION in V4R confirms right ventricular involvement.
Right ventricular infarction makes output preload-dependent; nitroglycerin can cause collapse. More elevation in III than II raises suspicion before V4R.
